**For Claude Design.** Small brief, high stakes. This is the highest-value undrawn screen in the set.

Referenced in doc 21 as `4a Home — first run`, specified but never drawn.

---

## Why this screen matters more than its size suggests

This is what a brand-new user stares at for the ten seconds after finishing onboarding, before their first photo. They have just answered ten questions and been given three numbers. They have invested effort and received nothing yet.

It is also what a returning user sees every single morning — every day starts empty.

Those are two different emotional moments wearing the same layout. The screen has to work for both.

## Two variants of the same state

### A. First run — no entries ever

The user has targets but has never logged anything.

Needs to answer, without a tutorial: *what is this app asking me to do?* The answer is one thing — photograph your food. Everything else can wait.

* The ring exists but is empty. It should read as "ready," not "broken"
* Targets are visible — this is the payoff of the ten questions, and it should feel earned
* Tiles read `—`, not `0`. Nothing has happened yet; zero is a measurement, a dash is an absence
* One clear invitation to log the first meal
* Optionally, a quiet second path: backfill from the photo library, for someone who already has today's lunch on their camera roll

Resist the onboarding-carousel instinct. One action, made obvious.

### B. Empty day — returning user, nothing logged yet today

Same skeleton, different feeling. This person knows what the app does.

* No explanation, no teaching
* Ring empty, targets shown, tiles `—`
* The log action stays exactly where it always is — muscle memory matters more than novelty
* A past day with nothing logged uses this same state, plus the option to backfill

The distinction from variant A is tone and the presence of guidance, not layout.

## Copy direction

`NOTHING LOGGED YET` is in the spec and works. It's factual and doesn't scold.

Avoid:

* Cheerleading ("Let's crush your goals today!")
* Guilt or urgency of any kind
* Anything implying the user is behind

The app's voice is a competent friend, not a coach with a whistle.

## Constraints

* Same layout skeleton as populated Today (`4a`) — this is a state, not a different screen
* Log food stays pinned bottom, identical position to the populated state
* Three macros: calories, protein, fiber
* No tab bar; `≡` menu top-left as everywhere else

## Edge case worth drawing

A past empty day reached via the calendar. Same state, but the log action means "backfill from library" rather than "take a photo" — you can't photograph yesterday's dinner today.

## The bar

A new user knows exactly what to do next without being told twice. A returning user feels the day is open, not that they're behind.
